The claimed span is printed verbatim on the page (left column, final paragraph): "In 2021 we supplied fresh, nutritionally-dense produce to 630 members over the span of 40 weeks... That's why in 2021 we offered: 60 free shares to refugee families in partnership with the Refugee Development Center, 38 subsidized shares for folks who were experiencing hardship, and 16 shares for folks who wanted to pay using SNAP benefits." Correct class is REJECT, not impact_story: the passage is a program description with aggregate distribution counts (630 members, 60/38/16 shares). Fields are faithful: title, primary_beneficiary (refugee families), and what_changed (60 refugee families received free fresh produce shares) all map accurately to on-page text and invent nothing — the error is purely the impact_story label. PII: the refugee/immigration framing is a sensitive_context flag; named entities on the page are corporate donors (AF Group, Emergent BioSolutions, Sparrow Health System, Magna Dexsys), not private named individuals, so no named_person; no specific minor is implied.

Against the three-part impact-story test: (1) Reyna is an identifiable speaker/participant — OK; (2) org intervention (the training/"work you do") is implied — OK; but (3) the "change" is only a vague, self-reported cognitive/attitudinal shift ("I learned how to... better understanding on my choice of words") wrapped in gratitude ("Thank you for the work you do. That is a TESTIMONIAL, not an impact story. The system's fields (title, beneficiary "Reyna, professional", what_changed) faithfully describe the on-page text without inventing facts. PII: only a first name in a testimonial attribution (treated as an unnamed-speaker characterization), no sensitive context, no minor — none.
